study type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) and observational studies
cohort: The study included data from 36 publications (11 RCTs and 25 observational studies) investigating outcomes in pregnant women undergoing elective induction of labor versus expectant management.
finding: RCTs suggest that inducing labor at 41 weeks or later reduces the risk of caesarean birth and meconium-stained amniotic fluid.
mod_finding: Inducing labor at 41 weeks or later was found to reduce the risk of caesarean birth compared to expectant management.
